references.text: Moses sets up a tent of meeting outside the camp as a place for God's presence, parallel to Peter's desire to set up tents for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah.
David expresses a desire to find a dwelling place for the Lord, which mirrors Peter's wish to make dwellings for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah.
Jeremiah refers to a time when people will come to stand before the Lord in the place He has chosen, which can be seen as a parallel to Peter's desire to establish a holy place on the mountain.
The entire event on the Mount of Transfiguration, where Peter wants to build tents, is part of this narrative.
Luke's version of the Mount of Transfiguration, where Peter also suggests building tents for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah.
Hebrews discusses Jesus as a high priest greater than Moses, which may provide background for why Peter wanted to build tents for both of them, as well as Elijah.
Revelation speaks of God's dwelling among people, which can be seen as a fulfillment of Peter's desire to build dwellings for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah.
